intended_object: Given a basis b of a K-vector space V and an index j, this is the homomorphism of group schemes V_a → G_a over Spec K that takes the j-th coordinate with respect to b, i.e. the projection Gₐ^n ≅ V_a → Gₐ in Milne 2.6. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the module documentation.
explanation:
In this library, the coordinate ring of V_a is Sym_K(V^*) and that of Gₐ is Sym_K(K) = K[t], with t = ι(1). The underlying Hopf-algebra map `vectorGroupProjectionBialgHom` is the symmetric-algebra lift of c ↦ ι(c · b.coord j). So it sends t to the dual-basis coordinate functional b.coord j, viewed as a linear polynomial function on V. The lemma `vectorGroupProjectionBialgHom_coordinate` confirms this.

The definition applies the Hopf-algebra-to-group-scheme functor `hopfSpec` to this bialgebra map. That gives a genuine morphism of group objects over Spec K, which is the j-th coordinate projection. On points it is x ↦ (b.coord j ⊗ id)(x), as the lemma `vectorGroupProjection_globalCoordinate` shows.

The field hypothesis is the library's ambient setting for vector group schemes, which use `Module.Dual`, so the definition is not too narrow. The index type is arbitrary (any `i : Type u`), not restricted to `Fin n`. Mathlib has no group-scheme counterpart of this map.
